e-3627.knowledge_point: Differentiating the Product of a Constant and the Natural Logarithm Function
e-3627.worked_solution:
The derivative of the natural logarithm is the reciprocal function:

$$
\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{ \textrm{d} x}\left( \ln x \right)= \dfrac{1}{x}
$$

We apply our formula and get

$$
\eqalign{
\dfrac{\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x}   & = \left(5\ln x\right)'\  
                                                    & = 5 (\ln x)'\
                                                    &=5\cdot \dfrac{1}{x}\
                                                    &= \dfrac{5}{x}.
						  

}
$$

e-3628.knowledge_point: Differentiating a Sum Containing a Natural Logarithm Function
e-3628.worked_solution:
Taking the derivative, we have

$$
\eqalign{
			f'(x) &= \left(2\ln x+x^2-1\right)'\
			&=2 \cdot \dfrac{1}{x}+2x-0\
			&=\dfrac{2}{x}+2x.

}
$$

after.problem: Given that $y=2{x}^{e}-ln⁡x$, find the instantaneous rate of change at $x=1.$
after.worked_solution:
To find the instantaneous rate of change at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

Taking the derivative, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{x}^{e}-ln⁡x) \\  & =2e{x}^{e-1}-\frac{1}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the instantaneous rate of change at $x=1$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=1} & ={(2e{x}^{e-1}-\frac{1}{x})|}_{x=1} \\  & =2e\cdot {1}^{e-1}-\frac{1}{1} \\  & =2e-1\,.\end{aligned}
$$
